title: Merge k Sorted Lists
oneLinerQuestion: Merge k sorted linked lists into one sorted linked list efficiently.
explanation:
Problem Intuition: The Merge k Sorted Lists problem requires combining k sorted linked lists into one consolidated sorted list. A brute-force linear search across all k list heads takes O(k) per node, totaling O(N * k) time (where N is the total number of elements). By utilizing a Min-Heap (Priority Queue) of size k, we can determine the global minimum among all active list heads in O(log k) time, yielding an optimal overall runtime of O(N log k).

- Step 1: Sentinel Dummy Node & Min-Heap Setup — We initialize a dummy head node 'dummy = new ListNode(0)' and a moving tail reference 'curr = dummy'. We also instantiate a min-heap configured to compare nodes based on their numerical value (node.val).

- Step 2: Seed the Min-Heap with List Heads — We iterate through the array of k linked lists and insert each non-empty head node into the min-heap. At any given moment, the heap holds at most k elements—precisely one representative head node from each currently active list.

- Step 3: Extract Global Minimum — While the min-heap is not empty, we extract the top element using 'minNode = minHeap.pop()'. By the heap invariant, this node is guaranteed to hold the smallest value among all remaining unprocessed nodes across all k lists.

- Step 4: Link Node & Replenish from Same List — We attach the extracted node to the merged list via 'curr.next = minNode' and shift our pointer forward with 'curr = curr.next'. If 'minNode.next' exists, we immediately push 'minNode.next' back into the min-heap, maintaining representation from that specific list without exceeding heap size k.

- Step 5: Termination & Result Return — Once the heap is completely empty, all N nodes have been extracted and chained in non-decreasing order. We return dummy.next, which points directly to the head of the final merged linked list.

- Complexity & Memory Guarantees — Time Complexity: O(N log k) where N is the total number of nodes across all lists and k is the number of linked lists, since each of the N nodes is pushed and popped from a heap of size at most k. Space Complexity: O(k) auxiliary space required to maintain the min-heap priority queue storing at most k pointers at any time.
pseudoCode:
FUNCTION mergeKLists(lists):
    minHeap = NEW MinHeap()
    FOR EACH list IN lists DO:
        IF list IS NOT NULL THEN minHeap.PUSH(list)
    END FOR
    dummy = NEW Node(0), curr = dummy
    WHILE minHeap IS NOT EMPTY DO:
        node = minHeap.POP()
        curr.next = node
        curr = curr.next
        IF node.next IS NOT NULL THEN minHeap.PUSH(node.next)
    END WHILE
    RETURN dummy.next
END FUNCTION
